modules.title: Generalization & Adaptation
modules.summary: Unseen compositions, dynamics shifts, task transfer, and adaptation.
modules.intro: World models encounter changes in object configurations, transition dynamics, observations, and goals. These papers study how learned structure transfers and how interaction history or parameter updates support adaptation.
modules.scope: Each entry specifies the tested shift and outcome. Prediction transfer, policy transfer, adaptation from context, and fine-tuning are different evaluation settings.
modules.connections:
HOWM and Dreamweaver study composition; WM3C uses language-guided causal components for unseen environments.

CaDM conditions dynamics on history, while Context and Diversity and Considering Context examine what that history reveals. Dynamics Are Learned shapes a trajectory embedding for policy adaptation.

Curious Replay changes the data used for updates; WOMBET generates source-task experience for target-task fine-tuning. Behavior-Invariant Task Representation Learning addresses changes in offline behavior and online interaction.

General agents need world models supplies a formal connection between goal generalization and prediction.

modules.title: World Model Interpretability
modules.summary: Physical variables, causal interventions, and interpretable model design.
modules.intro: Interpretability studies identify the variables represented by a world model and examine their role in prediction. Related model designs give latent variables explicit physical meaning.
modules.scope: Representation probes, interventions on model computation, behavioral tests of learned structure, and physically interpretable architectures provide different forms of evidence.
modules.connections: Interpreting Physics analyzes physical information in video representations. What Do World Models Learn in RL? extends probing and interventions to learned Atari simulators. What Has a Foundation Model Found? tests learned structure through adaptation to synthetic tasks, without identifying internal circuits. Four Principles for Physically Interpretable World Models introduces design constraints that align latent variables with physical meaning.

modules.title: Structured & Compositional Representations
modules.summary: Objects, relations, and modular transition mechanisms.
modules.intro: Object and relation structure factorizes a world model into entities and interactions. These methods infer interaction graphs, learn object-specific visual features, or restrict which components participate in a transition.
modules.scope: Structure may be supplied by the input, learned from observations, or encouraged by a prediction objective. Relation recovery and compositional transfer are reported as separate outcomes.
modules.connections: NRI infers relations between observed entities. C-SWM learns object embeddings and relational transitions from pixels. SPARTAN sparsifies context-dependent interactions to adapt to mechanism changes. Causal-JEPA makes missing object-level information the prediction target. HOWM and WM3C, listed under Generalization & Adaptation, directly evaluate how composable dynamics support new configurations or environments.

modules.title: Representation Geometry & Symmetry
modules.summary: Latent geometry, learned transformations, and symmetry-based dynamics.
modules.intro: Latent geometry and transformation structure determine which changes a world model can represent. These papers study geometric regularization, learned group actions, equivariant transitions, and dynamic memory under partial observability.
modules.scope: The comparisons distinguish supplied symmetry priors, learned observation mappings, and learned transformation parameters. Long-horizon prediction, equivariance probes, and downstream planning provide different tests of the resulting representations.
modules.connections: Group Structure learns latent transformations and disentangled subspaces from interaction sequences. Group-Structured Latent Space supplies the symmetry and latent manifold; SEN learns an observation mapping compatible with a prescribed latent group action. GRWM regularizes geometry and temporal context for deterministic rollouts. FloWM maintains moving spatial memory under partial observability, with long-horizon prediction, probes, and a planning experiment. These methods make different assumptions about known transformations and the information available in each observation.

groups.title: Learning group structure and equivariant transitions

modules.title: Planning & Task-Relevant World Models
modules.summary: Goal-directed prediction, task abstraction, and model-based action selection.
modules.intro: World models support action selection through predicted futures or representations that preserve decision-relevant quantities. These papers connect latent dynamics to planning, task abstraction, and task-agnostic experience collection.
modules.scope: The evaluation target can be goal-reaching, reward, or the quantities needed for policy evaluation. Task success is interpreted in the tested environment and transfer protocol.
modules.connections: DINO-WM plans in frozen visual features; V-JEPA 2 connects video pretraining to action-conditioned prediction and robot planning. JEPA-WMs separates encoder, objective, and planner choices. Denoised MDPs isolates controllable and reward-relevant factors, while Value Equivalence formalizes the model information needed for Bellman updates. Plan2Explore collects experience through disagreement between predictors before downstream rewards are specified.

modules.title: Evaluation & Benchmarks
modules.summary: Compositional prediction, physical inference, and closed-loop validity.
modules.intro: Evaluation connects a world model's predictions to explicit tests of generalization and physical inference. The protocols here cover unseen combinations, extrapolation, future events, hidden physical properties, and closed-loop outcomes.
modules.scope: Each protocol specifies what the model observes, what changes at test time, and which outcome is measured. World-model-based policy evaluation is included when correspondence with real outcomes is tested; adjacent policy-only simulation studies appear in Supplementary Reading.
modules.connections: SVIB tests unseen combinations in one-step visual prediction; A Physical Law Perspective isolates interpolation, extrapolation, and compositional physical prediction. Physion measures future object-contact judgments. Physion++ extends that family with events requiring inference of hidden physical properties. World-In-World compares world models in closed-loop tasks, whereas WorldGym checks whether policy outcomes and rankings in a learned environment agree with real-robot evaluations.

comparison_table.title: Evaluation targets
rows: One-step prediction on held-out factor combinations

Agreement with real policy success rates and rankings
Validity of a learned policy-evaluation environment

route.label: Interpreting Physics
route.connection: Introduces physical-variable probes and targeted interventions, establishing the kinds of evidence used to study a learned representation.

route.label: Probing RL World Models
route.connection: Applies probes and interventions to learned environment simulators, linking internal state to generated predictions.

route.label: What Has a Foundation Model Found?
route.connection: Tests proposed world structure through transfer behavior, complementing evidence from internal activations.

route.label: HOWM
route.connection: Defines object composition as an explicit generalization problem for reusable transition models.

route.label: WM3C
route.connection: Connects compositional mechanisms to language-guided factors and adaptation in unseen environments.

route.label: Symmetric Embedding Networks
route.connection: Shows how observations can be mapped into features compatible with known symmetries, providing a different source of reusable structure.

route.label: GRWM
route.connection: Relates geometric regularization and temporal context to deterministic rollout accuracy, alongside the explicit symmetry constraints in SEN.

route.label: Context and Diversity Matter
route.connection: Examines how interaction history and training diversity support inference in a new environment.

route.label: Dynamics Are Learned, Not Told
route.connection: Uses trajectory-derived context geometry to adapt policies to changed dynamics.

route.label: DINO-WM
route.connection: Connects action-conditioned latent prediction to planning and goal-reaching.

route.label: SVIB
route.connection: Makes the generalization split explicit by withholding combinations of familiar factors during training.

route.label: Physion++
route.connection: Tests whether observed interactions support inference of hidden physical properties needed for future-event prediction.

candidates.title: JEPA-Bisim: Learning Robust Visual Representations for Planning with Joint-Embedding Predictive World Models
aliases: Learning Invariant Visual Representations for Planning with Joint-Embedding Predictive World Models
candidates.method: Adds a bisimulation encoder to a joint-embedding predictive world model, placing states with similar transition dynamics near one another while suppressing task-irrelevant visual features.
candidates.evaluation: PointMaze and PushT experiments test planning under background changes and visual distractors with several frozen visual encoders. The reported robustness concerns these observation shifts.

resource_review.note: Code linked from the paper and matched against the author repository. Candidate status is unchanged.
